text:
rahul: Hey team, I'm stuck on a terraform plan in staging after I added a local_file resource for bootstrapping. Plan just sits at 'Refreshing state...' for >20m and doesn't error out. Anyone seen local_file cause refresh hangs with remote state?
infra-bot: Detected lock on backend table 'tfstate-locks' owned by session 'terraform-apply-6732' (age 28m). If stale, consider `terraform force-unlock <LOCK-ID>`.
elaine: local_file is local-only so it shouldn't be in remote state. Can you run `terraform state list | grep local_file` to confirm? Also check if any data sources reference the k8s provider - that can pull on the cluster during refresh.
rahul: Ran `terraform state list` — no local_file entry. Lock owner looks like a CI run that got stuck earlier. Tried `terraform force-unlock`, but the lock reappears immediately.
sam: CI runner could be retrying and re-acquiring the lock. Check the DynamoDB TTL and the CI job history. Also validate if the k8s provider is configured to use in-cluster creds — the provider refresh might be blocked by kube-apiserver slowness.
rahul: Good call — our kube API was flapping (noticed high latency). I terminated the hanging CI job and then ran `terraform force-unlock 7a3f2c1d-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-9f2b1c2d3e4f` to clear the stale lock.
infra-bot: Lock 7a3f2c1d-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-9f2b1c2d3e4f released.
rahul: After unlocking, plan moved but now it wants to replace a `kubernetes_namespace` and recreate a secret that we actually created manually last week. Looks like drift. Should I import or let terraform recreate?
jenny: If the secret was created outside TF and you want terraform to manage it, run `terraform import kubernetes_secret.my_secret default/my-secret` then `terraform plan`. If you want to keep the manual secret, consider `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [data] }` or remove the resource from config.
rahul: Imported with `terraform import kubernetes_secret.my_secret default/my-secret` and re-ran plan — changes are gone, plan is clean. Thanks everyone :tada:
elaine: FYI we should add a CI pre-check to bail if a lock is >10m stale and notify on the lock owner. Saves a bunch of manual poking.
sam: +1, maybe also surface kube api latency as a separate SLO so we spot this earlier.
rahul: Agreed, filing a quick ticket for the CI pre-check and kube SLO. Thanks! :thumbsup:
